C45221.observed: What was checked: that every bin a part is held in has a name and a count, and that exactly one of them is marked as the part's default bin. What happened: five stocked parts were looked at and all five behave the same way. Each carries a set of bins; every bin has a name - the ones seen were "Unassigned", "D1B" and "SHOP", so these are real named locations, not placeholders - and every bin has an on-hand count against it, including counts of 6, 4, 792, 0 and one that is already at minus 1. On each of the five parts exactly one bin, and only one, is flagged as the default.
C45221.not_observed: Every stocked part on this branch is held in a single bin, so a part with several bins - where 'exactly one default' has more to prove - could not be checked here.

C45239.observed: What was checked: what happens for a part that is not held in stock anywhere. What happened: a catalogue part was chosen - its card in the search list reads "Catalog" instead of showing a stock quantity and a bin, which is how you tell them apart - and a quantity was entered. No bin was allocated, no "Pulled from" line appeared under the row, and no bin chip was shown anywhere. That is right: there is no stock to pull from, so there is nothing to allocate.
